text: During declared grid stress events, participating large-load customers should reduce non-critical electricity demand by 15% for up to two hours while protecting critical customer-facing services.
Participants commit to curtail at least 2 MW of flexible AI training and batch load within 10 minutes of a utility dispatch instruction, for events lasting up to 4 hours.
Large-load customers shall reduce non-critical consumption by 10 percent when the grid operator declares an emergency. Production inference must not be interrupted.
Reduce load by 20% for three hours during grid stress. Important workloads should be preserved where reasonable.
Enrolled data centers agree to shed 12% of load for up to 90 minutes, pausing evaluation and synthetic data jobs first.
When prices exceed the threshold, throttle model training by up to 25% for two hours. Do not pause or stop any job.
The site will automatically reduce non-critical load by 8% for 60 minutes upon a declared grid stress event, protecting safety systems and customer-facing inference.
Reduce 15% for up to 2 hours during grid stress; respond within 15 minutes; embeddings and batch indexing may be delayed; training may be throttled; production inference is protected.

Shift at least 1.5 MW of deferrable AI compute out of the 4-hour peak window when requested by the utility, keeping latency-sensitive services running.
